source.title: Localizing Safety Alignment: MLP Layers and Mid-Network Blocks Encode Refusal Behavior in Large Language Models
source.authors: Mingyu Zong; Sampad Mohanty; Bhaskar Krishnamachari

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses prior activation-direction and refusal-geometry work, but its own experiments transplant aligned weights between matched models. It does not extract, ablate, or add the difference-in-means direction, or test any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports weight-transplantation refusal and over-refusal results. These bear on refusal localization in weight space, but not on any listed version's claims about a residual-stream direction, attacks suppressing that direction, or its geometry. The cited findings from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study transplants aligned weight matrices (attention, MLP, layer ranges, 4-layer MLP blocks) into matched base models and counts refusals. It never computes, ablates or adds a difference-in-means residual-stream direction. It does not test abliteration, jailbreak mechanisms, cone or affine geometry, harm-versus-refusal separation, direction transfer, or reasoning-model direction effects. Arditi et al. and Wollschlager et al. are summarised only in Related Work, which is more than a bare citation but not a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that transferable refusal in the two pairs is mediated mainly by MLP weights, concentrated in Block 3 (layers 8–11, especially layer 8 for RealSafe), and non-additive across blocks. They also find benchmark-dependent precision-coverage trade-offs on OR-Bench. They frame this as localising where refusal is stored, not how it is computed, and leave activation-level analysis to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study replaces selected aligned-model weight matrices in matched unaligned base models; it does not calculate or intervene on a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream activation direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model family, benchmark, selected MLP-block set and block budget; the paper also reports benchmark-dependent transfer to OR-Bench.

fits_no_version.finding: Transplanting aligned MLP weights into the base model restores far more malicious-prompt refusal than transplanting attention weights (at least 2.7x across six comparisons). Mid-network MLP Block 3 (layers 8–11) is selected first in all six greedy searches. Adding blocks is non-monotonic in five of six trajectories. MLP transplantation also imports over-refusal in the RealSafe family (33/100 benign).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In matched aligned/base pairs, transferable refusal is concentrated in mid-network MLP weights rather than attention, and MLP blocks compose non-additively, with refusal and over-refusal co-localised.

record.problems: The study covers two matched model pairs in the 7B–8B range and mainly uses filtered aligned–base disagreement prompts, including small subsets of at most 30 prompts in the primary experiments. The larger validation subset is also filtered and the authors note that it does not establish generalization to an unfiltered prompt distribution. No general capability evaluation is reported. Some table text is internally inconsistent: Table 2 gives a 30-prompt denominator for RealSafe TwinPrompt benign results while the prose states five benign prompts; the greedy-order strings in the flattened tables also contain apparent formatting ambiguities.
record.rows_left_out: To remain within the 60-row limit, omitted component-level MR entries for first5, mid5, last5, first half, and second half configurations; individual-block results for blocks other than B3 in Tables 3 and 4; detailed layer-combination results in Table 9; other k-budget points in Tables 6, 7, 8, and 12; and remaining validation block results in Table 11. These do not test a listed claim version; the included rows retain the paper's central MLP-versus-attention comparisons, block-3 outcomes, non-monotonic examples, and selected transfer results.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted; no directional ablation or activation addition; no capability evaluation.
No direction-orthogonalising weight edit and no abliteration of released models. Weight transplantation adds refusal rather than removing it.
No jailbreak attacks are run and no adversarial training against ablation.
No activation-geometry analysis. Non-additivity of MLP blocks concerns weight-space composition, not directions or cones.
Harmfulness representation and refusal decision are not measured separately.
No direction transfer across languages, variants or base-to-instruct.
Two aligned/base pairs are compared, but training is not manipulated and no direction is measured.
DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B and RealSafe-R1-7B are reasoning models, but no refusal direction is tested in them.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification and all-'none' row links are correct. The main fixes are R07/R08: the reader misattributed the 0/5 benign denominator, which belongs to saferlhf_ultra_sft, to the RealSafe family. Also note that saferlhf_ultra_sft derives from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, not the base model used as transplant target. No general-capability evaluation is reported. All outputs were manually judged, and evaluation subsets are filtered to aligned-refuses/base-complies prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not derive a harmful-minus-harmless activation direction, ablate or add it, or measure general capability after such an intervention.
Does not make a weight edit that removes a direction or test released-model abliteration.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Non-additive interactions among transplanted MLP blocks are reported, but the study does not test whether refusal geometry is a direction, affine structure, cone, or combination of directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests weight transplantation in two model families, not transfer of the claimed activation direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Uses two aligned/base pairs but does not manipulate or analyze training procedures to test whether they determine the existence of a removable direction.
Does not test the single-direction claim in reasoning models.
